challenges.attack: Shape-based acquired-callable analysis has propagation and call-site gaps
challenges.mutation_or_trace: Two distinct mechanisms are incomplete. Propagation: a container literal whose element is a fresh Call/Subscript/Attribute does not taint the container ((a(),1), [a()], {'k':a()}, {a()}), and destructuring (d, n = a(), 1), for/comprehension targets, function parameter defaults, decorator-rebound function names, with-as targets and except-as targets are not assignment forms _complex_callable_bindings considers. Call-site: even a correctly tainted name escapes when invoked through a container subscript ((d,)[0](x), [d][0](x), {'k':d}['k'](x)) or through d.__call__(x), because node.func is then a Subscript or an unlisted Attribute. Immediately-invoked expressions a()(s) and reg['k'](s) are likewise unreachable by the analysis.
challenges.expected_behavior: Taint containers whose elements are capability-shaped; treat For/comprehension/with/except targets and function parameter defaults as assignments; flag Call nodes whose func is a Subscript or Call, and add __call__ to the attribute check.
challenges.observed_behavior: No accepted shape can be supplied a genuine JSON decoder. All 22 producer compositions tested — json.loads reference, container of json.loads, functools.partial, lambda, default arg, class attribute, decorator, JSONDecoder().decode, numpy.load, mlx.core.load, bare o.loads — reject at the name-agnostic and json-capability layers. The gap weakens a forward-looking review aid, not the prohibition on the measured bytes.

challenges.attack: Support ledger v10 overstates shape-analysis coverage
challenges.mutation_or_trace: S-O-C06-001 evidence item 3 states the fixed-point analysis rejects invocation of callables acquired through 'Call, Subscript, Attribute, aliases, containers, conditional transport, named expressions, or class storage'. Containers are covered only for transport of an already-tainted Name; a container literal built directly from a Call is not tainted, and extraction from a tainted container is not enforced at the call site (see F-C07-001).
challenges.expected_behavior: Amend the S-O-C06-001 wording to state exactly which container forms propagate and which do not, so a future cycle does not rely on the broader reading.
challenges.observed_behavior: The overstatement is in evidence narrative, not in a claim. Every claim verdict here was re-derived independently from executed bytes rather than from the ledger text.

challenges.attack: R5 receipt v11 carries a stale commands_executed provenance line
challenges.mutation_or_trace: f017-v9-root-continuity-node-r5-receipt-v11.json records commands_executed ['gh run view 32882085157', ...] while result_counts.full_native_run_id is 32886210156. Run 32882085157 is the cycle-05 CI run at head 79367b50, copied forward from receipt v10; receipts v8, v9 and v10 each had matching pairs, so v11 is a one-field copy-forward regression.
challenges.expected_behavior: Correct commands_executed to reference 32886210156 in the next receipt bank.
challenges.observed_behavior: The substantive counts are correct and independently confirmed against the live GitHub API: run 32886210156 exists at 07ebd970, succeeded, with 4 required jobs passed and 0 native skips.

challenges.attack: from typing.<submodule> import bypasses the typing member vocabulary check
challenges.mutation_or_trace: The UNAUTHORIZED_TYPING_MEMBER_IMPORT gate keys on node.module == 'typing' exactly, so from typing.io import TextIO passes the vocabulary check while its import_root 'typing' is still approved.
challenges.expected_behavior: Key the vocabulary check on the import root rather than the exact module string.
challenges.observed_behavior: Not executable on the pinned runtime: CPython 3.13.13 reports 'typing is not a package', so any such import fails closed at import time. The dangerous typing members (get_type_hints, ForwardRef, evaluate_forward_ref, _evaluate) are also caught path-independently by CAPABILITY_REEXPORT_IMPORT.

challenges.attack: breakpoint() is an environment-gated in-process decoder not covered by DYNAMIC_BUILTIN_NAMES
challenges.mutation_or_trace: breakpoint is absent from DYNAMIC_BUILTIN_NAMES, so breakpoint(text) passes the policy. Verified on pinned CPython 3.13.13: PYTHONBREAKPOINT=json.loads python3.13 -c "print(repr(breakpoint('{\"a\": 1}')))" prints {'a': 1} — a genuine unbounded in-process JSON decode with no json token in the source.
challenges.observed_behavior: Requires operator-controlled environment rather than current bytes, and the independent closure census confirms no breakpoint/eval/exec/compile/__import__ name occurs in any of the 32 modules. Same family as the out-of-process inline decoders that item 11 directs be assessed separately.

challenges.attack: Out-of-process inline decoder commands remain unscanned
challenges.mutation_or_trace: subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-c', '...json.loads...']) and os.popen('python3 -c ...') both pass the policy; subprocess, os and sys.executable are all approved surfaces. Carried forward from O-C06-003.
challenges.expected_behavior: Semantic scanning of inline -c command strings, if this class is ever to be closed.
challenges.observed_behavior: Assessed separately per required attack 11. No current authority artifact is decoded through an external interpreter; the only subprocess decode in the closure is the offline qualify_f017_quantization_matrix_v1.invoke probe, unreachable from the active runtime.

challenges.attack: Hand-rolled structural decoding over approved ast.parse is undetectable by an AST policy
challenges.mutation_or_trace: ast is an approved root and ast.parse is not a capability attribute; a hand-written walker over the resulting tree could decode JSON-shaped text without eval, literal_eval or any json token.
challenges.expected_behavior: None available at the policy layer; note as a permanent limit of the approach in the bounded-decode contract.
challenges.observed_behavior: Requires authoring a parser, is absent from current bytes, and is not decidable by any AST-shape policy by construction. Structural, not a current-byte path.
